comments.author: @afti03
comments.text:
I used Gemini yesterday to help me change a title from "Study in the UK" to something more attractive. It proceeded to write almost a paper on the emotional side of people when reading certain words, ultimately giving me titles for each of the emotional categories I might want to explore (e.g., optimistic, intriguing, adventurous). 
Then, to my surprise, it actually generated three different types of responses with different tones! I read everything it came up with and was absolutely shocked. For comparison, I gave the same prompt to ChatGPT and GPT-4, and they both provided short answers with just a single title, "Unlock your career: Uk studies await." Interestingly, all three models - Gemini, ChatGPT, and GPT-4 - started with this exact title, with slight variations: Gemini's was "Unlock your career: Study in the uk," while ChatGPT offered "Unlock your career: Uk Studies." What truly impressed me was that Gemini offered at least 50 good titles to choose from.

comments.text: Unfortunately no matter how big the context window is the quality of output is reduced depending on how many words the model tries to squeeze the answer into. Lets say u are a researcher trying to collect information from sources and put 10k tokens in and ask it to extract all the points with no summaries, u still lose 70percent of the points and thats not including the fallibility of the models in expressing them accurately because it cant fit them all in its likely 1000 word response it will give you. We do need increased maximum outputs for performance increase else performance wont be increased unless we ask for very specific things
